purpose: Hit the ball back over the net with a controlled, repeatable groundstroke on the backhand side: turn the shoulders early, load the legs, meet the ball in front of the body with a stable base, and swing through to a full finish, so the ball lands in the target area with pace and control.

phases.description: Ready position at the start of the point: knees slightly bent, racket in front, weight on the balls of the feet.
Shoulders and hips turn together as the racket is taken back; the player steps and loads the legs.
Legs drive, hips then shoulders unwind and the racket accelerates up and forward to contact in front of the body.
Racket continues across and up to a full finish while the body stays balanced.
Return to a balanced ready position for the next ball.

objectives.goal: Turn the shoulders well past the hips on the takeback so the chest is turned away from the net.

below.looks_like: Arm-only takeback with the chest still facing the net; the swing is cramped and relies on the arm.

above.looks_like: Over-rotated, shoulders turned far past the hips, which makes the swing longer and harder to time.

objectives.cue_intent: Remind the player to turn the chest and show their back to the net early.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they feel their shoulders turn or mostly just take the racket back with the arm.
objectives.fix_intent: Have the player turn the shoulders as soon as the ball is read, with the racket going back as a result of the turn.

objectives.goal: Bend the front knee and sit into the legs at the end of the turn to load for the swing.

above.looks_like: Standing tall on straight legs, so the swing comes from the arm and the player cannot get under or drive through the ball.

below.looks_like: Sitting very deep, which slows the recovery and drive.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to bend the knees and get low before swinging.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they feel their legs working or if they stand up as they hit.
objectives.fix_intent: Use a shadow swing that starts with a pause in a lowered, loaded position.

objectives.goal: Set a stable, shoulder-width or wider base as the swing begins.

below.looks_like: Feet close together, narrow and unbalanced base that makes the player lose balance in the swing.

above.looks_like: Feet very far apart, restricting rotation and the weight transfer.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to step out and set the feet wider before hitting.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they were on the move or had time to set their feet.
objectives.fix_intent: Practise a split step followed by an open step into a stable base.

objectives.goal: Transfer weight forward into the shot so the body moves toward the target at contact.

below.looks_like: Leaning back on the heels at contact, producing short, weak or floating balls.

above.looks_like: Lunging forward too far, jamming the swing and losing balance.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to step and move the body into the ball.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they feel they fall back or stay on the back foot when hitting.
objectives.fix_intent: Drill stepping into the ball with feeds, finishing with the weight on the front foot.

objectives.goal: Meet the ball with the hitting arm comfortably extended out in front, neither cramped nor stretched.

below.looks_like: Arm jammed against the body because the ball is too close or the contact is late.

above.looks_like: Overreaching with a fully stretched arm, reducing control.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to give the ball space and hit it out in front.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the ball tends to feel too close or too far away at contact.
objectives.fix_intent: Adjust spacing with the feet before the swing so the ball is met at a comfortable arm's length.

objectives.goal: Keep the trunk steady, not collapsing sideways, through contact.

above.looks_like: Trunk tilting or falling away to the side, causing mistimed contact and loss of balance.

below.looks_like: Overly rigid upright posture with no bend to reach low balls.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to keep the head and chest steady through contact.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they feel off balance after hitting.
objectives.fix_intent: Practise holding the finish on balance for a count after each stroke.

objectives.goal: Swing through to a full, high finish with the racket across and over the shoulder.

below.looks_like: Abbreviated swing that stops at or just after contact, with the arms staying low.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to swing all the way through to a high finish.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they are stopping the racket after hitting the ball.
objectives.fix_intent: Use shadow swings that hold a full finish for a count.

outcomes.description: The ball is struck cleanly with pace and control and lands in the target area of the court.
The backhand is performed with sound, balanced technique, judged from the body alone.

links.mechanism: A full coil stores rotational energy that unwinds into the racket, while too little leaves only arm power.
A bent, loaded leg lets the player drive upward and forward through the ball and adjust to low balls.
Moving the body forward into the ball adds momentum and keeps contact in front.
The distance of the hand from the body at contact sets the contact point, affecting both racket speed and control.
A full finish shows the racket accelerated through the ball and promotes topspin and clearing the net.

session_ideas: Shadow-swing backhands in front of the camera from the side, five at a time, holding the finish.
Feed-and-hit drill with a partner or ball machine feeding to the backhand side.
Shadow swings pausing at the end of the unit turn to check shoulder turn and knee bend.
Drop-feed backhands focused on stepping into the ball.

vocabulary_proposals.name: racket
vocabulary_proposals.why: Racket head position and path are central to contact point, swing path and racket speed, but cannot be measured from body features.

vocabulary_proposals.name: ball
vocabulary_proposals.why: Ball position is needed to judge contact point and where the shot lands.

vocabulary_proposals.name: contact_point_in_front
vocabulary_proposals.why: Distance of the wrist ahead of the front hip at contact, a key coaching point not directly in the registry.

vocabulary_proposals.name: grip_type_one_or_two_hand
vocabulary_proposals.why: Whether one- or two-handed changes the expected wrist spacing and finish; dist.wrist_width only partly captures it.

vocabulary_proposals.name: head_stability
vocabulary_proposals.why: Coaches often say to keep the head still at contact, which requires a head-position feature.
